Flood Spread to the Gandak

Nepal Modelled Flood Movement and Spread

The flood released on the upper Trishuli moves down the Narayani valley and spreads across the floodplain before crossing into India at Triveni. Press Play to watch the ground it covers fill in red as the front advances. Zoom and pan the map to follow it reach by reach.

Possible Flood Spread Calculation

A spot turns red once the flood front passes the point on the main river it drains to, if its ground sits less than the chosen flood depth above the river. The shade shows water depth (flood depth minus ground height above the river), so it is darkest in the channel.

Flood depth at the main river
How high the flood water rises above the normal level of the Narayani. Ground that sits less than this height above the river gets wet, with the water shallower the further it is from the channel. Deeper water also moves faster, so this changes both how wide the flood spreads and when it arrives. Range 1–20 m.
Manning's roughness n
How much the riverbed and floodplain slow the water down: about 0.030 for a smooth open channel, up to 0.075 for rough, bouldery or vegetated ground. A higher value makes the flood arrive later. It does not change how much ground is flooded.

Viewing controls, not model inputs: Scrub the front moves the flood along its route and Playback sets the animation speed. On the map, scroll or pinch to zoom, drag to pan, and double-click to zoom in on a spot. IND jumps to the border crossing at the Gandak barrage, FIT shows the whole corridor, and Follow the front keeps the leading edge centred while it plays. Water is shaded by depth, deepest red in the channel.

Model limitations

  • No bank breaches: water only spreads over ground that drains back to the main river, not into neighbouring basins.
  • Flood depth is an input, not calculated: there is no discharge data to compute the real water level.
  • Timing is an estimate: arrival times assume a single flood wave, not days of monsoon rain and barrage releases.
  • Stops at the border: the elevation data ends at 27° N, so the flood's path through Bihar is not modelled.

Trunk-relative HAND and chainage labelling on a 60 m D8 grid, 13.9 M cells. Spread is encoded as one image — connection chainage in red, height above the trunk in green — so the browser can threshold it live on both time and flood depth. The 3D terrain view shows the same model in relief; the full model report covers validation and exposure.
